en: Oh, yes, Bean Paste Buns. Three of them.
And, I'll take two Pizza Buns. Oh, yes, the Bean Paste Buns, I asked for one too many. That'll be my order.
(So, how many of what did he want?)
By the way, do you carry postage stamps?
Postage stamps? Uh...
Ta-chan, we have those. We have two kinds, 50 and 80 yen.
Oh, okay. Got it.
Very well. May I have 390 yen worth of stamps?
(Uh, 390 yen worth would be how many 50 yen and 80 yen stamps?)
So, uh, that would be four 50 yen and three 80 yen stamps... I think?
Hm? No, that would add up to 440 yen.
Uh-oh, did I get it wrong? Uh, so 390 yen worth would be...
So, would that be three 50 yen and three 80 yen stamps?
Let me see... Ah, yes, that's right. That adds up to 390 yen.
Great! Your total comes to 1,270 yen. Thank you for shopping with us.
So, uh, that would be five 50 yen and two 80 yen stamps?
Hm? No, that would add up to 410 yen.
Uh-oh, did I get it wrong? Uh, so 390 yen worth of stamps should be...
Sorry. I'm still fumbling with the calculation.
Oh, that's fine. Please, take your time.
I'm so sorry. Okay, so 390 yen worth of stamps should be...
Way to go, Ta-chan! We finally got rid of that conniving kleptomaniac!

Heh, that was the easy part. Working behind the register was
way harder.

I know what you mean. You always have to be thinking ahead,
crunching numbers, anticipating all kinds of problems...
A lot's expected out of you for such little pay!
Right, that's only like 700 yen an hour... At least it's steadier work than my writing gig.
Wow, you freelance writers don't have it easy either, huh? Well, here's your pay.
You got a <Color:8>Tauriner +<Color:Default>.
You manned the counter like a veteran, too. You got it down, Ta-chan. Heck, I hope I can call on you as a pinch hitter if we're short-staffed.
Hehe, thanks.
You were pretty good behind the counter. Actually, you were great for your first time. Not bad at all, Ta-chan.
Well, it seems like you had some issues behind the counter, but nothing too major.
Today I learned I'm really not cut out for working at a convenience store.
I added a reward for catching that crook in with your payment, too. Oh, and don't forget your bento!
You got <Color:8>Expired Lunch Set<Color:Default>.
Woohoo! Thanks! I really needed this.
Hey, but this is a one-time deal, okay? Don't get it into your head that you can keep coming back for more.
Haha... You had to go and say that.
Anyway, you really came through today. Thanks a bunch, Ta-chan!

Gee, even you couldn't nab that crook? He sure is a slippery
one.
Sorry I couldn't come through for you. Especially after going through all that work at the register.

Yeah, how was that? It's a job that makes you think ahead
and keeps you calculating all the time. Not as easy as it
looks, is it?
They sure expect a lot out of us, despite the bullshit pay!
Wow, you freelance writers don't have it easy either, huh? Well, it's too bad you couldn't catch that crook, but here's your pay.
You manned the counter like a veteran, too. I think you got it down. Heck, I wish I could call on you as a pinch hitter if we're short-staffed.
You were pretty good behind the counter. Actually, you were great for your first time.
You couldn't catch the shoplifter, but you were helpful with the customers. So here, you still get this.
Woohoo! Thanks! I needed this.
Haha, as if.
Okay, thanks for helping. See you around, Ta-chan!
To be honest, I wish you would've been better behind the counter. I hate to do this to you, but I had to dock your pay.
I feel bad about that, so here, take this.
...And who are you?
Heh. Please don't tell me you forgot you promised this girl a date already.
What? You're the cho-han dealer?
Who else would I be? Or were you expecting someone else?
No, it's just that... You look different.
Heh. I'll tuck that away as a compliment. Okay, let's go.
Sure. Where to?
Where else? It's a nice place.
That didn't go well. At all.
Heh. Sometimes you're lucky, sometimes you're not. It's not your fault.
Thanks for keeping me company today. Take this, with my thanks.
I had a good time, but I have to go now. Drop by again to play cho-han, okay?
I've never won like this before. I can't believe it.
Feeling more confident now?
Much more confident... Thank you. I'm glad I asked you to help me.
Oh, that's right. We had a bet going. I won at roulette, but you clearly won our wager.
Here, I'll give you something nice. Can you close your eyes?
What for?
Just do it!
It's not much, but...
Heh. Couldn't have asked for a better tip.
Hmph! Well, that was fun, our date. Drop by for some cho-han again. See you.
A casino?
You're disappointed? Don't tell me you had your hopes up for something else.
It's not that. I was just surprised that you⑬the face of the gambling hall⑬would choose a casino.
There's actually a reason why I wanted to come here with you.
I live in the world of gambling. Above all, I'm a cho-han dealer. Like you said, I'm the face of the gambling hall.
So I have to be an expert in all kinds of gambling. That's what a pro does.
Despite all that... I just can't get a feel for roulette. Believe me, I played it a lot, but I can't seem to win.
I need to fill this hole in my repertoire. I want to feel confident about it. Of course, I can't say this to the boys at the hall.
And that's where I come in.
You catch on fast.
So what do you want me to do?
Well, I was hoping you could show me that it's actually possible to win at roulette.
Excuse me, sir. Would you care to play as the dealer?
Perhaps you could give a demonstration of your mastery to your guest.
Most certainly. After all, you are a valued regular of the Dragon Palace.
What do you think?
Heh. It sounds like a perfect opportunity. While we're at it, what do you say to a little wager?
You mean besides chips? What do you want to bet?
I'm going to bet three times. Let me win and get my confidence up. If you can do that... I'll give you something nice.
Fair enough. Let's do this.
You did it!

en: Heh, just glad to be useful.
You definitely were! And you helped a total stranger. I mean, I just don't have the words to thank you properly.
So instead, here's a small gift.
You got a <Color:8>Balance Bracelet<Color:Default>.
I screwed it up.
Well, the ramen was ruined, but I'm still grateful that you tried to help. Who does that for a complete stranger?
Eh, doesn't change the fact that I wasn't useful to ya.
You did your best! And it was useful because it gave me some faith in humanity.
So, here's a small gift.

Hurry to the customer eagerly awaiting a bowl of steaming hot ramen. <Color:255,200,200,255>Approach him gingerly<Color:Default>, for the roads are <Color:255,200,200,255>icy slick<Color:Default>, and a fall will surely spell the noodles' demise! <Color:255,200,200,255>Keep calm and carry ramen!<Color:Default>

Keep in mind, it's not just you facing the dangers of an icy road. <Color:255,200,200,255>Other people<Color:Default> may slip and slide, <Color:255,200,200,255>becoming obstacles that can knock you over<Color:Default>. Avoid these flailing victims of the streets!

Hurry to the fallen deliveryman, but since the road is <Color:255,200,200,255>dangerously slick with ice<Color:Default>, you should <Color:255,200,200,255>approach gingerly<Color:Default>! If you run, you might trip, which will just slow you down.
Made it! Are ya okay?
It doesn't matter. Right now, this ramen is more important.
Please, I know you don't know me, but could you deliver it? We're almost out of time!
Uh, how is this ramen more important than you bein' hurt?
Please! Please just help me!
Fine, but where'm I supposed to take it, exactly?
The customer is waiting at the corner over there.
Hey! Over here! Hurry it up!
Oh no, he's already annoyed. Please! Leave me behind. Just save the ramen!
Soon the noodles will get all soggy...
Okay, okay. I'll take care of this. But you need to relax, fella.
I can't, I'm still worried about you walking across this slippery road. If you fall, the ramen won't survive. Please be careful.
It'll be okay. The ramen's gonna make it.
Help! Somebody!
(Hm? What's goin' on?)
Please! Oh, please, in heaven's name!
(Is that... a delivery guy? He hurt or somethin'?)
(Wait a sec...)
(The road's completely coated in ice.)
Sir, are you coming to help me?
When I slipped, I landed awkwardly, and now I can't move.
Yeah, but I cross the street, I'm just as likely to wipe out. Whaddaya expect me to do?
Maybe if you just walk carefully...
I guess that is the only way, but...
Please! There isn't a second to waste!
Oh, all right. Guess I should help him.
(Matsuo Lamb Barbeque. This place oughta get Tatsuya's attention.)
(I gotta help out the delivery guy now.)
Gotcha. So you're hiding your past so it doesn't hurt Haruka-chan's chances of becoming an idol?
Yeah. Having me around would only cause her trouble. This was the only option.
Did you really need to take a new name, though?

But man, I had no idea what was going on. Sorry for running
my mouth and almost blowing your cover.
No need to apologize. I didn't expect to run into anyone I knew down in Fukuoka.
Yeah, talk about a coincidence.
What brings you out here anyway?
Oh, uh... I just came out here for vacation. Thought it'd be nice to get out of Kamurocho for a change.
Okay, but what about the club? Kazuki put you in charge, so I hope there's someone capable filling your shoes while you're gone.
Don't worry, Stardust is still standing. Besides... it's not like it'd fall apart if I just up and left.
Yuya. Are you really just here on vacation?
Huh? What kind of question is that?
I'm asking if there's any other reason you're down here. You're acting kind of evasive.
You can tell me the truth. I can't promise I can do anything about it, but I can at least listen.
...All right. But this is between you and me, okay?
Sure. I understand.
Actually, Kiryu-san, I'm thinking of quitting the host business.
(Is he serious!?)
Stardust practically runs itself these days. We have no shortage of rising stars on staff, and everything's going smoother than ever.

And the guys I once thought of as newbies are now fully able
to handle things on their own, so they hardly ever need my
advice.
As the years move on, I've started to get the feeling that I've lost my way. Kind of like something's missing in my life.
It was never like that before. I was always really driven to make Stardust a big success.
But now I don't have the same passion. I can tell it's all downhill from here.
Yuya...
So I thought I should put some distance between me and Stardust.
That seemed like the only way to find the fire that I used to have.
I see. And that's what brought you here, huh?
Haha... That's a thing, right? Going on a trip to do some soul-searching? That's pretty much what this is for me.
What about Kazuki? Didn't he leave Stardust in your hands?

I haven't told Kazuki anything. Not yet, anyway. It's hard
enough admitting how I feel to myself, let alone the guy who
gave me his business.
In any case, I'm useless to him the way I am now. If I had to go back like this, I'd be better off quitting.
Would you really go that far?
I can't go on like this, can I? Getting away from Kamurocho was all I could do to try and fix things, but I still don't know what to do with myself.
That said, running into you here has given me an idea.
I could start over in a new town, and become someone else. Like what you did here.
I want to make a fresh start, too! It'll be like the old days, when I still had the drive to make things happen. I think that'll help me get myself together!
And how do you plan to make a fresh start?
First, I'll find a job. It doesn't matter what it is.
Actually, I should probably find the kind of job nobody else wants to do. A job that forces you to work like crazy to get things done!
So you won't be going back to Stardust?
I don't think so, no.
I see. Kazuki won't be happy with me, but I don't think there's anything I can say to change your mind.
Thanks, Kiryu-san. I knew you'd get me!
Well, I'd better head off. I got some serious job hunting to do! Oh, and the udon was great!
(Udon West, huh? I could tell Tatsuya about this place.)
I need to apologize to you too, Kiryu-san. For crashing in on your new life. I guess I still have a long way to go as a leader.
